newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Angry Belgian Philips staff occupy plant.
newsitem.headline: Angry Belgian Philips staff occupy plant.

text.p: Staff at the Philips Electronics NV television plant in Bruges, Belgium, occupied the premises on Thursday in anger over job losses resulting from the restructuring of Philips television operations.
"We are not going to accept this," a union spokesman said.
Whether there would be any futher action by the union would be decided at a meeting on Monday, the union spokesman said.
The job cuts are part of a wider restructuring of the Sound and Vision division of the Dutch electronics group, which also affects sites in France and Italy.
The programme is due to cut the number of jobs at the Sound and Vision's Bruges, Dreux and Monza sites by 50 percent to around 1,400.
The union spokesman said staff were being unfairly treated. Staff levels were already cut in November 1995 when 70 jobs were lost.
Under the current plan 70 percent of blue-collar jobs were to go and one of three white-collar jobs, he said.

A Philips Bruges spokesman said Philips could not afford to make the same products at different places and noted that in the new strategy Philips Bruges had been assigned an "important and essential task", which was development and production.
In the restructuring Bruges is to become the world-wide colour television development centre with a production facility.
Philips said in July that developments in the consumer electronics industry meant that restructuring was necessary, especially in Europe.
Sound and Vision comprises television, audio, video equipment and interactive media systems.
Together with this latest restructuring some 2,500 jobs are being cut in the division's industrial activities in western Europe.
In July Philips said it would cut 6,000 staff from its Sound and Vision unit over 18 months.
Philips employs 270,000 people in 60 countries. The consumer products division, which includes Sound and Vision, employed a total workforce of over 70,000 as at end-June.
